result.title: ArtKit: Motion-Driven Re-Segmentation and Link Re-Generation for Articulated Objects from RGB-D Video
result.summary: An RGB-D camera that films an object being moved, often from one viewpoint, sees one side of it and how its parts move. We present ArtKit, which takes such a video as input to create an articulated model with complete parts, a kinematic tree, and typed joints. Our central idea is generating the hidden geometry and verifying it against what the camera sees. A generative part prior proposes complete, part-decomposed geometry based on the first frame. Point tracks, grouped into rigid trajectories, split and merge the generated parts into links. We then fit revolute and prismatic joints, with a visibility-aware energy ensuring that the articulated model explains the depth observed across the video. A rule checks against the video to choose between synchronous group fits and per-frame chain fits, so that one pipeline serves a diverse range of articulated objects, such as household items and robotic hands. Finally, we regenerate each link of the chosen fit as one part and keep it wherever it agrees better with the observations. We evaluate on Articulate-100 and on HArt, a new benchmark of 60 PartNet-Mobility objects and 8 robotic hands and grippers rendered as RGB-D videos with ground-truth parts and joints. ArtKit reduces the axis and part motion errors of the strongest baseline by more than half on the objects, as well as the axis error on the hands. ArtKit also runs on real recordings and generated videos.

AI.brief_summary: ArtKit 以单视角 RGB-D 视频为输入重建带完整部件、运动学树与关节类型的铰接物体：用生成式部件先验补全不可见几何，借点轨迹分组拆分合并为 link，再拟合旋转/平移关节，并用规则在多种拟合与逐 link 重生成结果间择优。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「先提出候选几何、再用可见性加权的观测一致性验证与择优」的流程，可能为 LVR 中多 latent 假设的视觉证据筛选与贡献判定提供概念参照，但该文属三维铰接重建，不涉及推理状态或答案生成，需核查借鉴价值。
